The description appears to come from a CBP ruling on a garment with a deep back opening, an attached cape, and raw, unfinished sleeves and hem. That sounds like a costume or a hospital or patient gown, and I can't confirm which. The raw edges and the hook-and-loop closure at the back suggest a disposable or single-use item such as a salon or examination cape or gown. It could also be a Halloween costume, which would fall under 9505.

A "cape" attached to a garment with sleeves and a back opening suggests a Halloween costume such as a superhero or vampire. Costumes made of non-woven or knit fabric with raw edges are often classified in 9505.90.6000 (festive articles, other). Under Note 1(e) to Section XI, however, carnival costumes of textile are excluded from Chapter 61 and 62 only if they are not garments of those chapters. Chapter 95 Note 1(e) excludes only "fancy dress of textiles, of chapters 61 and 62." CBP typically classifies costumes made of cheap, unfinished fabric in 9505.

The raw, unfinished edges are a classic feature of costume rulings, which describe a costume as "not finished" and therefore not wearing apparel. I'll go with 9505.90.6000.
